records.title: After the feet
records.prose:
The feet went away. I heard them getting smaller, then nothing. Kept my teeth out.

When I closed my mouth, I felt that I had let something in. Opened it again. Nothing came. I wanted to put my chin down, but I could not make myself do it.

Backed into the narrow place beside the wood until the earth touched both my shoulders. Stayed there. After a while I could close my mouth.

records.title: What I walked past
records.prose:
I stepped over the dead frog on my way to the water.

There was a live one at the edge. I waited until he stopped moving. Hopped nearer. He vanished on the first hop. A little farther along, another gave me just enough time to spread my wings. I landed where he had been sitting. Water ran off a stone.

The dead frog was still there when I came back. Picked him up. Carried him toward the bank, where I could watch for another live one.

I had begun waiting again when I tried to open my bill. The frog was in it. I would have to put him down before I could catch anything.

Took him to a rock instead. Put a foot on him and ate. A frog jumped below me while I was eating. I watched where he went. Kept eating.
records.identityEvidence: Adult female in fiction. Photograph records do not establish sex or exact adult age.
records.visibleScene: A raven stands on a rock with a dead, dirt-covered frog in its bill.
records.fictionBoundary: The source explicitly shows a raven carrying a scavenged frog on a rock. Two failed hunts, walking past the carrion, returning to the bank, the occupied-bill realization and eating are fiction around acquiring this visible meal. The frog is already dead throughout. There is no false death, resurrection, memorial or invented prey suffering.
records.creator: NPS / Jacob W. Frank
records.canonDisposition: Can serve as Maud’s first adult narrative if lead admits it; her portrait already passed Bird25 lead review but the identity is not yet admitted. No mate, chicks or dependence on held aerial pursuit. The event tests her desire for command: she notices that pursuing a successful catch is keeping her from a meal already obtained. Medium profile is a proposed format addition, not a runtime change.
